issue: After Kisor v. Wilkie, must a federal court defer to the Sentencing Guidelines commentary and application notes only if the Guideline itself is genuinely ambiguous, or does Stinson deference continue to apply?
provision: U.S.S.G. commentary and application notes (Stinson v. United States, 508 U.S. 36 (1993); Kisor v. Wilkie, 139 S. Ct. 2400 (2019))

sides.position: Kisor's more demanding deference standard applies to Guidelines commentary; a court may defer to commentary only if the Guideline is ambiguous, so Stinson deference is no longer the standard.
cases: United States v. Riccardi, 989 F.3d 476 (6th Cir. 2021)
United States v. Castillo, 69 F.4th 648 (9th Cir. 2023)
United States v. Scheu, 83 F.4th 1124 (9th Cir. 2023)

sides.position: Kisor does not apply to the Guidelines; courts continue to apply Stinson deference to the Guidelines commentary.
cases: United States v. Moses, 23 F.4th 347 (4th Cir. 2022)

this_court: Adopts the Kisor side: the Ninth Circuit agrees that the more demanding Kisor standard applies to Guidelines commentary, following its earlier decision in Castillo.
quote: Since Kisor was decided, a circuit split has arisen over whether this more limited deference should apply to the Sentencing Guidelines commentary and application notes.
cite: United States v. Joshua Scheu, 83 F.4th 1124 (9th Cir. 2023)
